extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, quality reporting staff, health IT vendors, PPS-exempt cancer and long-term care hospital stakeholders, and commenters on the CMS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and implementation guidance for proposed CMS rule changes to hospital quality reporting programs (IPPS Hospital Inpatient QRP, PCHQR, LTCH QRP, and Medicare Promoting Interoperability), associated measure adoptions/removals/modifications, burden estimates, and regulatory analyses for notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM adoption (Hospital Inpatient QRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Advance Care Planning electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in section IX.B.1. of the preamble; adoption has no change in information collection burden in some contexts; also proposed for PCHQR and the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program (EHR reporting period CY 2028).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Harm-Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) eCQM adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE eCQM beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination (also proposed for EHR reporting period CY 2028).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would replace two process eCQMs (VTE Prophylaxis and ICU VTE Prophylaxis), potentially reducing administrative burden by replacing two process measures with one comprehensive outcome measure; would be available for self-selection and would become mandatory if the proposal to require Hospital Harm eCQMs after two years of self-selected reporting is finalized. See sections IX.B.1., IX.C.3.b., IX.C.4., and IX.F.9.b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess Days in Acute Care After Hospitalization for Diabetes measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Excess Days in Acute Care After Hospitalization for Diabetes measure beginning with the July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 performance period (associated with the FY 2029 payment determination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among new measures proposed for Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program; burden estimates for program-level changes are provided elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital 30-Day All-Cause Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following AMI measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Acute Myocardial Infarction Hospitalization measure for the July 1, 2024–June 30, 2026 performance period (FY 2028) through July 1, 2027–June 30, 2029 (FY 2031).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five mortality measures proposed for adoption; see preamble listing of five specified mortality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital 30-Day All-Cause Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Heart Failure measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Heart Failure Hospitalization measure for the July 1, 2024–June 30, 2026 performance period (FY 2028) through July 1, 2027–June 30, 2029 (FY 2031).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five mortality measures proposed for adoption; listed in preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital 30-Day All-Cause Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Pneumonia measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Pneumonia Hospitalization measure for the stated performance periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five mortality measures proposed for adoption; see preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital 30-Day All-Cause Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following COPD measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Hospitalization measure for the stated performance periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five mortality measures proposed for adoption; see preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital 30-Day All-Cause Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following CABG Surgery measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) Surgery measure for the stated performance periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five mortality measures proposed for adoption; see preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify Excess Days in Acute Care after Hospitalization measures (AMI, HF, Pneumonia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify three measures beginning with the July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026 performance period (FY 2028): (1) Excess Days in Acute Care after Hospitalization for Acute Myocardial Infarction; (2) Excess Days in Acute Care after Hospitalization for Heart Failure; (3) Excess Days in Acute Care after Hospitalization for Pneumonia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications are proposed as part of the broader measure updates; changes may affect performance period specifications and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove VTE Prophylaxis eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the VTE Prophylaxis eCQM beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination (and similar timeline for Promoting Interoperability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is linked to adoption of the Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE outcome eCQM; removal may reduce redundancy and administrative burden because the outcome measure could replace process measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Intensive Care Unit VTE Prophylaxis eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the Intensive Care Unit VTE Prophylaxis eCQM beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See guidance under Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE adoption about replacement and burden effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy eCQM beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the set of VTE-related process eCQMs proposed for removal in favor of an outcome eCQM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update Maternal Morbidity Structural measure reporting/submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose an update to the reporting and submission requirements for the Maternal Morbidity Structural measure beginning with the CY 2026 reporting period/FY 2028 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change affects how hospitals submit data for this structural measure; see referenced section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reporting of Malnutrition Care Score eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require mandatory reporting of the Malnutrition Care Score eCQM beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination (modifies reporting/submission requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also proposed to modify reporting/submission requirements across programs (Hospital Inpatient QRP, PCHQR, Promoting Interoperability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require mandatory reporting of Hospital Harm eCQMs after 2 years self-selected reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require mandatory reporting of Hospital Harm eCQMs after 2 years of self-selected reporting beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During initial years, hospital can self-select; after 2 years the Hospital Harm eCQMs would become mandatory if finalized; CMS provided Collection of Information burden estimates reflecting this possibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCHQR: adopt Advance Care Planning and Malnutrition Care Score eCQMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt two measures for PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital Quality Reporting beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 program year: (1) Advance Care Planning eCQM; (2) Malnutrition Care Score eCQM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no financial impact to Medicare reimbursement if a PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital does not submit data; administrative costs include implementing and maintaining EHR measure specifications; transition to FHIR-based eCQMs is intended to promote interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCHQR: remove COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among Healthcare Personnel measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among Healthcare Personnel measure beginning with the CY 2026 reporting period/FY 2028 program year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS does not believe removal would result in additional economic impact beyond collection-of-information estimates; removal reflected elsewhere in burden tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH QRP: remove HCP and Patient/Resident COVID-19 vaccine measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among Healthcare Personnel measure and the COVID-19 Vaccine: Percent of Patients/Residents Who Are Up to Date measure; if finalized, effective beginning with the FY 2028 LTCH QRP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates an overall decrease in burden for LTCHs participating in the LTCH QRP (summary: decrease of 4,473 hours and $207,309.29 for 318 eligible LTCHs); CMS seeks public comments specific to the estimates and on future measure concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH QRP: revise data submission deadline for LCDS assessment and CDC NHSN data
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise the data submission deadline for LCDS assessment and CDC NHSN data for the LTCH QRP (details in IX.E.6.b.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change is part of burden and timeliness improvements; CMS solicits comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Promoting Interoperability: adopt/remove/modify measures and attestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to adopt three new measures for EHR reporting period CY 2028: Advance Care Planning eCQM; Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE eCQM; Unique Device Identifiers for Implantable Medical Devices measure (also Unique Device Identifiers begins CY 2027). Propose to remove two attestations (ONC Direct Review Attestation; optional ONC-ACB Surveillance Attestation) and five measures (Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information; Support Electronic Referral Loops by Receiving and Reconciling Health Information; VTE Prophylaxis eCQM; ICU VTE Prophylaxis eCQM; Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy eCQM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose to update Electronic Prior Authorization measure by modifying ONC certification criteria to attest “Yes,” change measure text, make it an optional bonus for CY 2027 and required for CY 2028, and modify Malnutrition Care Score and Hospital Harm eCQM reporting requirements. CMS estimates net decreases in information collection burden for the program (3,886 hours saved; $213,982).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace Support Electronic Referral Loops measures with HIE Bi-Directional Exchange or TEFCA measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removal of Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information and Support Electronic Referral Loops by Receiving and Reconciling Health Information measures beginning CY 2028; eligible hospitals/CAHs would report either the Health Information Exchange (HIE) Bi-Directional Exchange measure or the TEFCA measure instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes potential onboarding labor and vendor costs for planning, procuring, configuring, validating workflows, and recurring costs (subscription, transaction, vendor maintenance). CMS lacks sufficient insight to quantify costs and seeks public comments describing direct costs and benefits associated with HIE or TEFCA adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to FHIR-based eCQMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Intend to transition to a fully digital quality measure landscape by transitioning eCQMs to Health Level 7® Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources® (FHIR®)-based eCQMs to promote interoperability and increase the value of quality measure data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition discussed in IX.D.5.b.(1). and in PCHQR discussion; administrative costs to implement and maintain measures in EHRs are multifaceted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative cost considerations for adopting/maintaining eCQMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative costs include burden associated with reporting and costs associated with implementing and maintaining program requirements, such as maintaining measure specifications in hospitals' (and PCHs') EHR systems for the eCQMs used in respective quality reporting programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS repeatedly notes that administrative costs are multifaceted and beyond simple information collection burden, including EHR configuration, vendor costs, and ongoing maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated information collection burden changes by program
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS provides quantitative estimates of changes in information collection burden for proposed policies: e.g., Hospital Inpatient QRP: increase of 8,133 hours ($447,803); PCHQR: increase of 15 hours ($826) and estimated decreases of 88–99 hours ($4,972–$5,801) in some contexts; Medicare Promoting Interoperability: decrease of 3,886 hours ($213,982); LTCH QRP: decrease of 4,473 hours and $207,309.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates are presented in summary tables in section XII.B. and related subsections; readers referred to detailed Collection of Information discussion in section XIII.B.7. and other sections for calculations and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for outcome measures over process measures to reduce administrative burden
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS rationale that replacing two process eCQMs with a single comprehensive outcome eCQM (e.g., for VTE) would reduce administrative burden and better capture harm outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated in multiple sections (e.g., IX.B.1., IX.C.3.b., IX.F.9.b.); outcome eCQMs may be voluntary initially and then required after a transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alignment with current clinical guidelines as a criterion for measure retention/removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination to remove COVID-19 vaccination measures for LTCH QRP was based on finding that these measures no longer align with current clinical guidelines and therefore may not reliably inform consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in 'Alternatives Considered' as a substantive standard for whether to retain measures; CMS cites lack of well-defined parameters for receiving vaccination when originally adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and actionability of publicly reported data as a criterion (submission deadline change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to shorten LTCH QRP assessment data submission deadline from 4.5 months to 45 days based on reasoning that 45 days gives LTCHs reasonable time to submit and correct data and increases timeliness/actionability for consumers and quality improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered keeping the deadline unchanged but concluded 45 days is reasonable; cited benefits: timelier data, increased value for consumers and LTCHs' quality improvement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid target price instability as criterion for payment model parameter selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering removing the 3 percent cap on the retrospective trend factor for TEAM, CMS worried that removing the cap would introduce target price instability and present challenges for participants to predict performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stability/predictability concern is used to justify retaining caps or constraints in payment model design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of public comments on proposals, alternatives, and cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS explicitly solicits public comments on proposals, alternatives considered, burden estimates, assumptions (e.g., number of reviewers), and costs/benefits of HIE/TEFCA adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple solicitations across sections (e.g., LTCH QRP burden estimates, HIE/TEFCA costs, TEAM alternative options); commenters are encouraged to address methodological assumptions used in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review cost estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: For estimating regulatory review costs, CMS assumes the number of reviewers equals the number of unique commenters on last year's proposed rule (5,409), assumes each reviewer reads ~50% of the proposed rule, uses BLS wage data for medical and health service managers (Code 11-9111) at $113.42/hour (including overhead/fringe), and estimates ~17.42 hours to read half the rule, yielding cost per reviewer of $1,975.78 and total cost $10,686,994.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS acknowledges uncertainty in this approach, invites comments on the assumption, and notes possible understatement/overstatement due to reliance on past commenter counts and reader behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) small entity analysis criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines small entities per SBA/NAICS standards (use NAICS code 622 'Hospitals' with $47 million size standard) and treats roughly half of hospitals as small entities; considers economic effects 'significant' when more than 5 percent of providers incur impacts of at least 3–5 percent of total revenue or costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies these criteria to estimate impacts on small entities (e.g., estimating number and revenue share of small IPPS hospitals and LTCHs, calculating approximate dollar impacts per small entity) and invites public comment on its initial regulatory flexibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates analysis threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, CMS assesses anticipated costs/benefits and notes the 2026 threshold for mandates requiring spending is approximately $193 million (in 2026 dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether additional analysis under UMRA section 202 is required.
